page: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit arm64 AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 4 physical cores mapped directly to 4 vCPUs at 1 thread per core. Memory capacity measures 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor contains 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes no integrated GPU hardware and has no local instance storage, depending entirely on networked block storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark profiles indicate performance consistent with burstable ARM architectures. The instance delivered a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.58 within the median 50% category, alongside a multi-core score of 6011.97. Geekbench results include 934.0 for single-core and 3173.0 for multi-core performance, reaching 4410.0 in software compilation and 2389.0 in image processing. The memory subsystem demonstrated solid uncached transfer rates, reaching 66.09 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 32.48 GB/sec for writes. Application benchmarks registered Redis throughput at 4.28 million operations per second and static web throughput at 4.66 GB/sec.

Given its burstable CPU allocation model, t4g.xlarge offers efficient resource utilization for workloads characterized by idle periods and periodic processing spikes. It represents a practical fit for microservices, development and test environments, web application hosting, build servers, and small transactional databases. However, applications requiring sustained, uninterrupted multi-core computational saturation will face performance tradeoffs once burst credits are depleted.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit arm64 AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration supplies 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It features no local storage and zero GPUs, relying on external storage volumes and offering a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-core stress-ng throughput (1519.58) and solid uncached memory bandwidth (66.09 GB/sec read, 32.48 GB/sec write), counterbalanced by modest multi-core compute and PassMark scores. This profile delivers cost-efficient compute density tailored for bursty workloads, intermediate microservices, web serving, code compilation tasks, and staging environments that do not require continuous full-core CPU saturation.
